column1: # WolOS console hints (ADR 0032 "Console"). `wol hint` prints a row's sentence and suggestion when a
# command is missing or fails in a way WolOS knows; every WolOS shell reads the first column once at
# start, so a command not named here never starts `wol`. One row per line, four columns separated by
# one tab: command, condition, sentence, suggestion. The first row that matches wins.
# command: the program name as typed (its last path part; a `wraps` command's line is looked up as the command behind it too).
# condition: words that must all hold; `!` in front of one means it must not:
#   missing      the command is not installed (the shell's command-not-found)
#   failed       it ran and its exit status was not 0
#   arg=PATTERN  one of its arguments matches; last=PATTERN: its last argument does
#   typed=PATTERN the command word as typed (/usr/bin/pacman, not pacman)
#   sealed       the system files are read-only (a WolOS slot, not developer mode)
#   nowheel      the account is not in the administrators' group (wheel)
#   managed      an argument names a service in /usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/50-wolos.preset
#   wraps        the command runs the rest of the line (the administrator word): the line is looked
#                up as that command too. Never matches, so it is not a hint of its own.
#   PATTERN: `*` is any text, `|` separates choices.
# sentence, suggestion: {cmd} the command, {args} all its arguments, {targets} the ones that are not
# options, {names} the targets after the first (apt install NAME), {first} the first target. An empty
# Translations: hints.<lang>.tsv beside this file (hints.pt_BR.tsv, then hints.pt.tsv, from LC_ALL,
# LC_MESSAGES or LANG), the same first two columns as the key; a row it lacks stays in English.
# Wording (UX-LESSONS): what happened and what to do, for a person, no blame, no jargon.
